conflicts.type: source-mismatch (not a formula conflict, but a research caution)
conflicts.description: A same-brand, similarly-named hautschutzengel.de page for 'MONDAY HAIRCARE Smooth Antifrizz' turned out to be the shampoo, not the mask, and was excluded rather than used or merged.

MONDAY's general brand marketing (seen across multiple MONDAY product pages/retailers, not confirmed specifically on this SKU's own packaging text) emphasizes 'silicone-free' formulas, but the confirmed INCI for this specific mask contains Dimethicone, Dimethiconol, and Amodimethicone - three silicone ingredients. This may be a brand-wide claim that does not apply to every SKU, or a genuine claim/formula mismatch. Not resolved this pass; flagged for the classification standard's claim-vs-INCI discrimination logic (this is exactly the kind of case F-rules are meant to catch).

statusNotes: INCI sourced via database aggregation rather than a single verbatim retailer fetch (hautschutzengel had the wrong product, dm.de/Rossmann.de both blocked) - moderate confidence. The silicone-free marketing claim vs confirmed silicone-heavy INCI is a genuine, notable discrepancy worth flagging to the orchestrator, independent of source-tier concerns.
